entities.name: Agustin Roman
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agustin Roman (1928–2012) was a Cuban-born Catholic bishop who served as Auxiliary Bishop of Miami, becoming the spiritual shepherd of the Cuban exile community in the United States and one of the most beloved figures in the Cuban-American Catholic world. Born in Cuba, he was ordained a priest in 1959—the year of the Cuban Revolution—and left Cuba in the early 1960s, eventually settling in Miami where the largest Cuban exile community was concentrated.

Roman was appointed Auxiliary Bishop of Miami in 1979 and served in that role for the rest of his active ministry. His primary apostolate was to the Cuban exile community, for whom he became a figure of profound spiritual and cultural significance. He served as rector of the Shrine of Our Lady of Charity of El Cobre—the patroness of Cuba—in Miami, a site that became the spiritual centre of the exile community and a repository of its collective memory and longing for a free Cuba.

Throughout the Castro decades, Roman maintained the exile community's faith and hope for Cuba's liberation. His ministry at the shrine attracted millions of Cuban-Americans over his lifetime. He witnessed the Mariel Boatlift of 1980 and subsequent waves of Cuban refugees, welcoming each new arrival into a community sustained by Catholic faith and national identity. At his death, he was mourned as a father figure by the entire Cuban exile community.
